platform.name: MilcharSec
platform.description: An interactive web-based cybersecurity learning and awareness platform designed specifically to help non-technical users understand, recognize, and respond to common cybersecurity threats.
target_audience: Individuals seeking to improve digital and workplace cybersecurity awareness

tracks.title: Digital Security Basics
tracks.description: A complete eight-module learning path covering cybersecurity fundamentals, account security, phishing, safe browsing, data privacy, mobile & remote work, incident reporting, and business email security.

modules.title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
modules.why_this_matters: Cybersecurity is not only the responsibility of an IT or security team. Everyday actions—opening an email, choosing a password, sharing a file, connecting a device, or clicking a link—can either reduce risk or create an opportunity for an attacker.
modules.learning_outcome: After completing this module, users should understand the purpose of cybersecurity and recognize common digital threats.
modules.interactive_activity: CIA Triad Challenge (Scenario-based analysis of email data sharing, grade manipulation, and server availability)
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Ali accidentally sends a confidential customer spreadsheet to the wrong external email address (Confidentiality impact)
Scenario: Someone secretly changes student grades inside a database (Integrity impact)
Scenario: Server becomes unavailable and employees cannot access a spreadsheet (Availability impact)
Scenario: Financial bank detail change request from regular supplier (Fake Invoice Scenario)

modules.title: Password & Account Security
modules.why_this_matters: Your online accounts are often the gateway to your personal information, academic records, communications, files, and other digital resources. An attacker does not always need to break into a complicated system. Sometimes, obtaining or guessing a user's password is enough.
modules.learning_outcome: Users should understand how to create and maintain stronger and more secure accounts.
modules.interactive_activity: Password Strength Checker exploration and Build a Better Account simulation
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Phone alert requesting verification code after unexpected IT call
Scenario: Spotting warning signs in a high-urgency account deletion notification
Scenario: Investigating a login notification alert from an unfamiliar, unrecognized device

modules.title: Phishing & Social Engineering
modules.why_this_matters: Attackers do not always need to break through sophisticated technical defenses. Sometimes, they try to manipulate people into making the security mistake for them.
modules.learning_outcome: Users should be able to recognize common phishing and social-engineering indicators.
modules.interactive_activity: Spot the Phish simulated email analysis & Phishing and Message Checker text testing
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Student account suspension warning email asking for password/MFA within 15 minutes
Scenario: Direct message claiming bank closure unless link clicked immediately
Scenario: Voice call claiming suspicious account activity and requesting OTP
Scenario: Director requesting urgent confidential report bypass procedures

modules.title: Safe Browsing & Device Hygiene
modules.why_this_matters: Your browser and devices are constantly connected to the digital world. Every day, you may visit websites, download files, install applications, open documents, connect to Wi-Fi, log into accounts, receive notifications, and update software. These everyday activities can introduce security risks when performed without enough caution.
modules.learning_outcome: Users should be able to recognize potentially suspicious websites and maintain better device security practices.
modules.interactive_activity: Website Investigation scenario and URL Safety Checker domain analysis
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Selecting video-editing software from official developer vs. premium-unlocked random site
Scenario: Analyzing a look-alike domain university-login-example.com for credentials risk
Scenario: Facing a pop-up alert warning of 12 device viruses requesting software installation
Scenario: Applying operating system settings update alert vs. random download updater site

modules.title: Data Handling & Privacy at Work
modules.why_this_matters: Information is one of the most valuable assets in an organization. Everyday work involves customer information, student records, financial files, internal communications, passwords, and contracts. A security incident does not always require malware or hacking. Accidentally sending the right information to the wrong person can also become a serious security and privacy incident.
topics: Sharing information with the correct recipient
modules.learning_outcome: Users should understand how improper handling of data can create cybersecurity and privacy risks.
modules.interactive_activity: Choose the Correct Data Classification challenge and Wrong Recipient simulation
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Sending a customer spreadsheet to accounting@example.net instead of accounts@example.com (Wrong Recipient)
Scenario: Accidentally selecting Reply All to a group email with confidential details attached
Scenario: Managing sharing configuration on a folder of confidential files set to 'Anyone with the link can view'
Scenario: Handling a colleague's/friend's unauthorized request to view confidential records out of curiosity

modules.title: Mobile & Remote Work Security
modules.why_this_matters: Cybersecurity does not stop when you leave the office. Today, people access organizational systems from smartphones, tablets, laptops, home networks, and public Wi-Fi. Working outside a traditional office can create additional risks because devices may be lost, stolen, connected to unfamiliar networks, or used around other people.
modules.learning_outcome: Users should understand how to maintain cybersecurity while using mobile devices or working remotely.
modules.interactive_activity: H.O.M.E. and D.E.V.I.C.E. routine mapping challenges & Permission evaluation
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Evaluating permissions (mic, location, camera, contacts) requested by simple flashlight app
Scenario: Connecting to faked or unverified public Wi-Fi networks in hotels/cafes (Hotel_Guest_WiFi)
Scenario: Shoulder surfing threats in crowded cafes during confidential doc access
Scenario: Handling unlocked laptop in public space while stepping away to order coffee
Scenario: Immediate reporting process when a corporate laptop containing sensitive credentials goes missing

modules.title: Security Incident Recognition & Reporting
modules.why_this_matters: Not every cybersecurity problem requires a technical expert. A normal employee, student, or user may be the first person to notice something unusual. Recognizing warning signs early and reporting them correctly can help an organization respond before the situation becomes more serious. The goal of this module is not to turn non-technical users into forensic investigators.
topics: What information should be included in a report
modules.learning_outcome: Users should understand when a cybersecurity issue may require reporting and what their role should be during an incident.
modules.interactive_activity: Incident Report Assistant reporting simulation & Incident recognition exercises
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Differentiating normal events (expiring password prompt) from incidents (unsolicited password change confirmation)
Scenario: Handling unexpected account password resets and spam MFA push notification requests
Scenario: Reacting appropriately to malware detection alerts without attempting manual fixes or security software deactivation
Scenario: Creating a high-signal report (What, When, Where, Who, How, Actions taken) rather than guess-based reports

modules.title: Email & Business Communication Security
modules.why_this_matters: Email is one of the most important communication tools used by organizations. Because email is so widely used, attackers often target it. A malicious email may attempt to steal credentials, deliver malware, redirect payments, obtain confidential information, or impersonate an executive.
topics: Safe use of CC and BCC
modules.learning_outcome: Users should understand how to communicate securely and identify common email-based business threats.
modules.interactive_activity: Email Verification domain inspections & Red Flags detection simulated challenges
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Unexpected attachment from look-alike email claiming to be your manager sending a PDF
Scenario: Supplier invoice received requesting bank routing modifications (Fake Invoice check)
Scenario: Executive impersonation (CEO) request to purchase gift cards urgently while in a busy meeting
Scenario: Detecting look-alike domains (company-example.com vs company-examp1e.com)
Scenario: Evaluating the security risks and access control limits of CC and BCC fields

modules.title: Women's Digital Safety & Online Privacy
modules.why_this_matters: Women's digital safety is essential for ensuring confident, secure participation in digital life. By understanding how to protect personal information, secure accounts, and respond effectively to threats like harassment or online blackmail, users can maintain control over their digital identities and privacy.
modules.learning_outcome: Users will be able to recognize common digital risks, implement robust privacy controls, and apply a structured response model when facing online safety incidents.
modules.interactive_activity: Privacy Setting Simulator & Fake Profile Awareness Checker
practical_scenarios: Scenario: Discovering an impersonation account on social media
Scenario: Receiving a blackmail threat involving private content
Scenario: Identifying indicators of AI-manipulated media

tools.name: Password Strength Checker
tools.description: Users can test password strength and receive detailed educational feedback explaining factors such as length, repeated patterns, predictability, and complexity without permanently storing any entries.

outputs_provided.weaknesses_identified: Array of specific layout issues found

privacy_rules: The system should not permanently store user passwords.
Checker should evaluate the password locally or process it temporarily without retaining original values.
Instruct users to enter fictional test passwords (e.g., Training-Example-Only-2026!), never real passwords.

tools.name: Phishing & Message Checker
tools.description: Users enter or paste a suspicious message, email content, or SMS. The tool evaluates potential phishing or social engineering indicators to output risk insights and recommendations.

outputs_provided.detected_indicators: Array of flagged techniques (e.g., urgent language, sensitive requests, impersonation, suspicious links, threat/fear, social engineering)
outputs_provided.explanation: Detailed rationale on why the context triggered specific indicators
outputs_provided.recommended_safe_action: Clear guidance on how to safely respond to or report the message

privacy_rules: Users must not paste real passwords, MFA codes, banking details, or other sensitive personal info.
Fictional or sanitized examples must be used for training.

tools.name: URL Safety Checker
tools.description: Analyzes an entered website address to inspect structural indicators of suspicion (such as protocol usage, domain layout, subdomains, IP usage, keywords, and look-alike domains) and return an educational assessment.

outputs_provided.detected_indicators: Array of flagged structure traits (HTTPS usage, suspicious URL structure, IP-address-based URL, excessive or misleading subdomains, suspicious keywords, look-alike patterns)
outputs_provided.educational_assessment: Explanation of URL components and common hijacking methods

privacy_rules: Do not enter passwords, MFA codes, private account info, confidential URLs, or sensitive organizational information.

tools.name: Cybersecurity Quick Check
tools.description: A platform-wide cybersecurity awareness diagnostic tool. Users answer targeted habit and awareness questions to evaluate their security habits and identify overall training recommendations.

outputs_provided.recommended_modules: List of learning modules mapped to weak categories

weak_area_identification.rules: Analyse user quiz and scenario results under each category. Any category displaying a score below the benchmark or significantly below other categories triggers weak-area status.

recommendations.trigger_basis: Weak-area status triggers an automated targeted suggestion pointing to corresponding corrective content.
